_comment: Calibrated parameters for shadow_range.py. Produced by grid search against clean midweek mfr_snapshots rows (Tue-Fri, width 1-30% of price, equities only), 41 tickers across 11 GICS sectors, 1282 reference rows over 2026-06-02..2026-07-24. Regenerate by re-running the calibration when the reference set materially changes.
_shadow_failover_note: Kill switch. true = names with no usable MFR range (dark / stale / validation-flagged) publish the shadow band tagged 'shd'. Set false to pull every shadow range back out of the reports with no code change. Applies to equity and ETF only - futures/crypto/fx are stored as status=class_uncalibrated and never fail over, because these params are equity-fit. Hedgeye (hdg) levels in hedgeye_risk_ranges are never touched by this: hierarchy stays hdg > mfr > shadow.

reference.filter: midweek Tue-Fri (excludes weekend carry-forward), width 1-30% of price, equities only

fit_quality._note: Edge MAE ~1.7% and rp MAE ~0.17 are the vendor-noise floor, not model error. MFR price vs yfinance close differs by a median 0.447% (p90 2.24%), which passes through roughly 1:1 into band-edge error. Calibration already matched mean band width exactly (1.45x -> 1.00x); the residual is dispersion. An implied-vol width driver was tested and REJECTED: R^2 iv 0.536 vs realized 0.758, blend 0.765 with a negative iv coefficient (collinearity, corr(iv,sigma)=0.885), and residual width disagreement is uncorrelated with the iv-rv spread (0.016).

validator._note: Empirical, set at p95 of the observed shadow-vs-MFR divergence on the clean midweek reference (NOT the shipped defaults of 0.25/2.0, which flagged 22% of known-good rows). Per-metric flag rate ~4.9%; combined either-flag rate ~8.6% - that is the expected false-positive floor, so a run flagging under ~9% of names is showing NORMAL disagreement, not feed trouble.
